title: Copilot connector setup: external connection and schema for HR policies
summary: Microsoft Graph connector starter: request bodies to create an external connection and register a labeled schema with searchable, queryable, retrievable and refinable properties for Copilot grounding.
body:
Concept and starter calls for a Copilot connector (Microsoft Graph connector) that makes an HR policy portal searchable and citable in Microsoft 365 Copilot. A connector needs three steps: create the external connection, register the schema, then ingest items. This entry covers the first two with the exact request bodies; the third step is in the companion entry on item ingestion. The schema is where Copilot quality is decided: semantic labels (title, url, lastModifiedDateTime) tell Microsoft 365 what the properties mean, and a short description on queryable properties helps Copilot map questions to properties. All IDs and URLs are placeholders.

=== Request 1: create the connection ===
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections
Permissions (application or delegated): ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy. The response is 201 Created with state draft and a configuration that lists the authorized app IDs.
{
 "id": "contosopolicies",
 "name": "Contoso HR policies",
 "description": "Indexes HR policy documents from the policy portal so that Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft Search can find and cite them."
}

=== Request 2: register the schema ===
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/contosopolicies/schema
Same permission. The call returns 202 Accepted with a Location header that points to an operation; poll it until the schema registration has finished. The schema must exist before the first item is added.
{
 "baseType": "microsoft.graph.externalItem",
 "properties": [
  {
   "name": "policyTitle",
   "type": "string",
   "isSearchable": true,
   "isRetrievable": true,
   "labels": [
    "title"
   ],
   "description": "Official title of the HR policy."
  },
  {
   "name": "policyUrl",
   "type": "string",
   "isRetrievable": true,
   "labels": [
    "url"
   ],
   "description": "Link to the policy page in the policy portal."
  },
  {
   "name": "lastModified",
   "type": "dateTime",
   "isRetrievable": true,
   "isQueryable": true,
   "isRefinable": true,
   "labels": [
    "lastModifiedDateTime"
   ],
   "description": "Date when the policy was last changed."
  },
  {
   "name": "department",
   "type": "string",
   "isQueryable": true,
   "isRetrievable": true,
   "isRefinable": true,
   "aliases": [
    "dept"
   ],
   "description": "Owning department, for example Finance, People or IT."
  },
  {
   "name": "regions",
   "type": "stringCollection",
   "isQueryable": true,
   "isRetrievable": true,
   "isRefinable": true,
   "description": "Countries or regions where the policy applies."
  },
  {
   "name": "effectiveDate",
   "type": "dateTime",
   "isQueryable": true,
   "isRetrievable": true,
   "description": "Date from which the policy is in force."
  }
 ]
}

=== How to use ===
1. Register an app in Microsoft Entra ID, grant it the ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy and ExternalItem.ReadWrite.OwnedBy application permissions and obtain a token with the client credentials flow.
2. Send request 1 and keep the connection ID stable; it is what a declarative agent references later in its GraphConnectors capability.
3. Send request 2, read the Location header and poll the operation until it succeeds before you add items.
4. Decide per property: searchable (full text, string types only), queryable (KQL filters), retrievable (returned in results) and refinable (filters and refiners).
5. Continue with item ingestion, then test with questions in Microsoft 365 Copilot and with the Microsoft Search results page.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Using names with spaces, symbols or more than 32 characters. Property names and aliases are alphanumeric and limited to 32 characters.
- Making numbers or dates searchable. Only string and stringCollection properties can be searchable.
- Skipping labels. Without title and url labels the results look anonymous and Copilot cannot cite them well.
- Adding items before the schema operation has finished.
- Registering more than 128 properties; a schema accepts between 1 and 128 properties.
- Trusting the baseType text blindly: the Learn schema resource page and the create-schema example differ here. This entry follows the create-schema example (microsoft.graph.externalItem); check the current page before you ship.

title: Copilot connector item ingestion with ACLs and a declarative agent that uses it
summary: Graph connector item PUT request with acl, typed properties and content, plus the v1.9 declarative agent manifest that scopes an agent to the connection through a GraphConnectors capability.
body:
The third connector step: ingest one item with its access control list, then let a declarative agent search the connection. The item is written with a PUT to the connection's items collection. acl is required and decides who can see the item in Copilot answers; properties must match the registered schema; content is optional full text that is indexed. A GraphConnectors capability in the declarative agent manifest (schema v1.9) scopes the agent to the connection through connection_id. IDs, groups and URLs are placeholders.

=== Request 3: put one item ===
PUT https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/contosopolicies/items/POL-0042
Permission: ExternalItem.ReadWrite.OwnedBy (application or delegated). Success is 200 OK. The payload is limited to 30 MB. Comment: non-ASCII strings need a type specifier (policyTitle@odata.type String) and every collection needs one (Collection(String)); for Collection(DateTime) use Collection(DateTimeOffset).
{
 "acl": [
  {
   "type": "group",
   "value": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111",
   "accessType": "grant"
  },
  {
   "type": "externalGroup",
   "value": "contractors",
   "accessType": "deny"
  }
 ],
 "properties": {
  "policyTitle": "Reisekostenrichtlinie",
  "policyTitle@odata.type": "String",
  "policyUrl": "https://policies.contoso.example/travel-expenses",
  "lastModified": "2026-09-01T08:00:00Z",
  "department": "Finance",
  "regions@odata.type": "Collection(String)",
  "regions": [
   "DE",
   "AT",
   "CH"
  ],
  "effectiveDate": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z"
 },
 "content": {
  "value": "Travel expenses are reimbursed within 30 days when receipts are uploaded to the expense tool. Hotel rates above the city cap need pre-approval.",
  "type": "text"
 }
}

=== File: declarativeAgent.json (agent that uses the connection) ===
Comment: connections without extra filters give the agent the whole connection. Optional filters such as additional_search_terms (KQL) or items_by_path narrow the scope.
{
 "$schema": "https://developer.microsoft.com/json-schemas/copilot/declarative-agent/v1.9/schema.json",
 "version": "v1.9",
 "name": "HR Policy Finder",
 "description": "Finds and cites current HR policies from the policy connector.",
 "instructions": "Answer only from the indexed HR policies. Cite the policy title and its link, mention the effective date, and say when no policy matches the question.",
 "capabilities": [
  {
   "name": "GraphConnectors",
   "connections": [
    {
     "connection_id": "contosopolicies"
    }
   ]
  }
 ]
}

=== How to use ===
1. Call PUT once per source document, using a stable item ID such as the document number, and repeat the call to update an item.
2. Map source permissions to acl entries: grant users or groups from Microsoft Entra ID with type user or group, and use externalGroup entries only if you created external groups for the connection.
3. Send dates as ISO 8601 strings and send collections with their type specifier.
4. Add the declarative agent to an app package and test with a user who is in the granted group and one who is not; the second user must not see the policy.
5. Schedule a crawl job that adds, updates and deletes items so that the index follows the portal.

=== Common mistakes ===
- Ingesting items with an empty or too broad acl and leaking restricted content into Copilot answers.
- Sending properties that are not in the schema or with the wrong type.
- Forgetting the @odata.type specifier for non-ASCII text or collections.
- Using the sample deny entry for externalGroup without creating that external group first.
- Assuming the agent sees the connection automatically. The agent must list it in GraphConnectors, and the user needs access to the content.
